subject: Post-demo recap — monthly burn velocity, slab options & PO thresholds
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Gill <sara.gill@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap — monthly burn velocity, slab options & PO thresholds

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and two asks so we can align commercial options with procurement expectations: 

Summary from our call:
- Expected monthly inference volume: ~1.2M – 2.5M tokens (mainly chat + lightweight summarization flows).
- Primary constraint: procurement requires PO routing and prefers consolidated monthly invoices.
- Legal lead time likely ~3–5 weeks per your note; SOC2 evidence already requested by your team.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm the target monthly budget band you expect to allocate to LLM inference (ballpark is fine: $Xk–$Yk / month)?
2) What procurement threshold requires a formal PO (e.g., > $25k, > $50k)? Any other vendor onboarding constraints we should know about?

Attached I’m sending a lightweight pricing model (pricing-model.xlsx) with three options we discussed: usage-based, light committed slab (monthly commit), and reserved capacity commit. The document includes per-1M token math for each tier — my working target for discussion is $95–$120 / 1M tokens on a starter committed slab depending on volume and term.

Next steps: if you can confirm budget band and PO threshold, I’ll pull together a short proposal + SOW draft and loop in our procurement lead for a sync. Would Tuesday or Wednesday next week work for a 30-minute procurement alignment?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — monthly burn velocity, slab options & PO thresholds

Alex — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget band: we’re planning an initial allocation of $100k – $150k / month (Q1 pilot). That should cover the expected 1.2M–2.5M token range with buffer for spikes.
- Procurement threshold: any vendor spend > $50k requires a formal PO and finance approval. Below $50k we can do a PCard or shorter purchasing flow.
- Legal/onboarding: 3–4 weeks is accurate; we need SOC2 Type II evidence and a data processing addendum (DPA) in place.

We’re excited to keep moving — Tuesday 11/09 at 10am PT works for a procurement sync on our side. I’ll invite our procurement lead (procurement@brightlinehealth.com) and legal depending on the agenda.

Thanks, Sara
Sara Gill
Head of ML Products, Brightline Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Gill <sara.gill@brightlinehealth.com>, procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — monthly burn velocity, slab options & PO thresholds

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Sara — perfect, that band is helpful. Based on $100k–$150k / month and the token range you gave, I sketched three commercial paths in the attached pricing-model.xlsx (revised):

Option A — Usage-based (no commit)
- Sticker: $150 / 1M tokens (streaming + chat profile)
- Pros: easiest procurement, no term
- Cons: higher unit cost, variable month-to-month spend

Option B — Starter committed slab (3-month term, monthly invoice)
- Commit: 1M tokens / month (prepaid credit), blended rate: $110 / 1M tokens (effective)
- If actual >commit, overage charged at $135 / 1M
- PO requirement: monthly invoice; finance signs PO > $50k (ok for your cadence)

Option C — Reserved capacity (12-month committed)
- Commit: 2M tokens / month, blended $85 / 1M tokens
- Includes 1:1 onboarding session and access to Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching & quantization

Quick math examples (from sheet): at 1.5M tokens/month — Option B ~ $165k/month (if overage hits), Option C ~ $127.5k/month. Given your $100k–$150k band, Option C with a 12-month commitment lands inside the band at the 1.5–2.0M range.

Procurement notes:
- If PO > $50k is required, we can route a monthly PO for Starter slab; for Reserved 12-month we typically do a single annual PO plus monthly invoicing (flexible).
- Legal/DPA: I’ll attach a SOW and a standard DPA for initial review (SOW-draft.pdf). We can also provide SOC2 evidence via our security portal prior to legal signature.

Next steps: I’ll bring a one-page commercial summary to the procurement sync on Tue 11/09 at 10am PT. Karthik, would you attend to speak to commit economics and whether we can offer a first-year onboarding discount? Sara — does Brightline want finance + legal on the call? If so, we’ll schedule a 45-minute slot.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/BRG-3419 (proposal draft in progress)

Thanks — Alex

Attachments: pricing-model.xlsx (revised), SOW-draft.pdf (stub)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — Brightline budget band & PO >= $50k (quick ask)

Karthik / Lauren — short internal note following Sara’s reply:

- External asks: Brightline expects $100k–$150k/mo, PO required for spend > $50k, legal lead time 3–4w, SOC2 & DPA required.
- Recommendation: offer Option B (Starter committed slab) as the default procurement-friendly path, and position Option C (12-month reserved) as the efficiency play.
- Commercial ask: can we pre-authorize a 15–20% first-year discount on top of the Starter slab rate for strategic pilots (deal BRG-3419)? This would move effective $/1M closer to $90–95 on 12mo.

Please advise: if legal needs a separate DPA template or if we should push for a single annual PO for reserved — I’ll reflect that on the procurement call. Karthik, can you join Tue 11/09 10am PT to present the commit economics?

— Alex
